Customer has strict security needs (KMS, RBAC, audit logs) and wants a pilot for bursty API traffic with predictable SLAs. AE + SE covered Console flows, API examples, and Optimize recommendations; agreed next steps for pricing, security docs, and a 50 RPS pilot.
topics: Org vs Project keys and mapping
Private deployment / KMS and SSO concerns
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-05
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez (Redwood); Ava Patel, Liam O'Neill, Samuel Reed, Nora Kim, Ethan Brooks (PrismWare)

Summary: quick runthrough of key hierarchy and access guardrails, demo of Console + API patterns, deeper notes on security integration and pilot next steps.

00:00 - Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, i'm the ae on this account. can you all hear me ok?
00:07 - Ava: yep, good to go. thanks, maya.
00:12 - Liam: afternoon team, liam here. we wanted to focus on how keys and quotas map to our org structure, and the security side.
00:21 - Maya: great, we'll start with a brief overview then diego will jump into the console and api patterns.
00:28 - Diego: hi all, diego se here, i'll show a couple of live flows: creating org keys, scoping project keys, and applying quota slices. i'll also demo fairshare and sticky routing briefly.
00:41 - Samuel: quick note — we need kms integration, audit logs, and sso via saml. also curious about role based access for key creation.
00:50 - Maya: absolutely, that's in scope. we'll show where RBAC lives in the console and how audit logs surface.
01:05 - Diego: ok i'm sharing my screen, first slide is key concepts: org key is top-level identity for billing and global quotas, project keys are scoped to teams or products, you can attach quota profiles to either.
01:25 - Nora: so project keys can have burst capacities separate from org defaults?
01:30 - Diego: yes, you can override at the project level; think of org as a bucket with a global quota and projects as sub-buckets with their own steady-state and burst allowances.
01:44 - Liam: how do you handle sticky routing? we have geo and latency sensitive services.
01:50 - Diego: sticky routing pins a project or org key to specific capacity lanes — region, model variant, or dedicated cluster. if the primary lane is saturated Redwood will gracefully failover to a fallback model or region based on policy.
02:08 - Ava: can we prioritize latency-sensitive traffic over background embedding jobs?
02:14 - Diego: yes, priority lanes and dynamic fairshare let you assign weights; latency-critical requests get higher share and lower queuing.
02:28 - Samuel: what's the unit for quotas — requests, tokens, concurrency?
02:33 - Diego: you can set quotas by tokens, requests, or concurrent sessions. typical pattern is token and concurrency for generation workloads.
02:46 - Ethan: our traffic is spiky — lots of short bursts from webhooks, then quiet. how does Redwood avoid penalizing us on cost?
02:54 - Diego: we recommend project-level burst buckets plus prefix/KV caching on common prompts. Optimize suggests quantization profiles and batching thresholds to save tokens and GPU time.
03:12 - Maya: we'll pivot to the Console demo now, diego?
03:17 - Diego: yep, opening the Redwood Console. first the org overview — here you can see top-line quotas, consumption heatmap, and active keys.
03:29 - [screen gesture] there's a table of keys, you can create an org key or a project key, attach an SSO group or service principal, and set RBAC roles.
03:42 - Nora: does creating a project key require enterprise plan or is it available to hosted?
03:48 - Diego: project keys are available across hosting modes. Dedicated and Private give more isolation controls — like enforcing VPC-only egress and customer KMS.
04:06 - Liam: for private deployments, how is KMS handled? we use AWS KMS with strict rotation policies.
04:12 - Diego: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and key wrapping. we can integrate with AWS KMS or an on-prem HSM depending on your deployment.
04:22 - Samuel: what about audit logs retention? compliance wants 12 months at a minimum.
04:27 - Diego: audit logs are configurable; enterprise tenants can set retention to 12/24 months and stream to your S3 or SIEM.
04:36 - Ava: show me how you'd map our teams — we have infra, product, and marketplace — to keys and quotas.
04:44 - Diego: you could create an org key for PrismWare, then project keys: infra-project, product-project, marketplace-project. set marketplace to lower steady-state but higher burst if you expect traffic spikes.
04:59 - [timestamp skip, demo continues]
06:05 - Diego: now the policy editor — you can write simple JSON policies or use policy templates. here's a rate policy that enforces a global per-org token budget and per-project concurrency caps.
06:21 - Liam: is policy evaluation at the edge? what's the latency impact?
06:27 - Diego: policy checks are lightweight and colocated with routing; typical added latency is <5ms.
06:34 - Samuel: can we integrate with our IDM for role sync?
06:39 - Diego: yes we support SAML for SSO and SCIM for user/group provisioning. you can map groups to RBAC roles in the console.
06:49 - Ava: you mentioned KV cache earlier — does that live in the serving lane or as a shared cache?
06:55 - Diego: prefix/KV caching is part of the serving runtime and can be per-customer or shared depending on isolation settings. for Private, you get dedicated cache that doesn't mix tenants.
07:08 - Maya: switching to API examples, i'll paste a sample curl showing how to issue a project key and attach quota profile.
07:18 - Diego: note the header X-Redwood-Project-Key and the quota-profile id. if you rotate keys you can issue a new project key and retire the old one without downtime using key aliases.
07:34 - Nora: do we get webhook notifications on quota exhaustion?
07:38 - Diego: yes, you can configure alerts, webhooks, and create fallback rules that route to a lower-cost model or queue requests.
07:48 - Ethan: curious about cost controls — can we set hard caps to avoid runaway bills?
07:53 - Maya: you can apply hard caps at org or project level; when hit, requests are blocked or redirected to a cheaper model, depends on policy.
08:06 - [dialogue and live demo interplay]
10:12 - Diego: quick aside on Optimize — it analyzes your prompt and recommends batching and quantization. for your embed-heavy jobs, it suggested an 8-bit quantized variant that reduced token cost by ~40% in our tests.
10:29 - Liam: cool, do you have sample results?
10:33 - Diego: yes i'll attach a short benchmark CSV after the call; for the pilot we'll run the same harness against your sample prompts.
10:42 - Samuel: security — can we require KMS-wrapped keys for all project keys?
10:46 - Diego: yes, for Private and Dedicated we can enforce key wrapping and rotation policies. Hosted can also support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations with extra controls.
10:58 - Ava: would like to see an example of tenant isolation in Console.
11:03 - Diego: switching to tenant view — here's a project isolated lane, it's pinned to a dedicated fleet, see the capacity lanes and current utilization.
11:14 - Nora: if a project exceeds its burst bucket what happens?
11:18 - Diego: it falls back to org-level quota or to a queued state depending on your failure policy; for critical services we recommend a fallback to a cheaper but compatible model for graceful degradation.
11:29 - Maya: any questions on routing or failure modes?
11:32 - Liam: how do you measure per-request latency across the stack for our dashboards?
11:36 - Diego: we emit per-request traces and token-level timing. Console shows p50/p90/p99 and tail latency. you can also export traces to your tracing backend.
11:50 - Samuel: what's the on-call escalation path for blips in dedicated capacity?
11:55 - Maya: Dedicated includes a support SLA and on-call escalation; we'll include the support plan in the SOW.
12:05 - [30-minute mark passed, mid-demo questions]
20:02 - Diego: jumping ahead, here's a policy template for rate-sculpting — it uses fairshare with weights per project and a burst quota that refills on a sliding window.
20:18 - Ethan: can weights be dynamic? like change during business hours?
20:23 - Diego: yes, policies support schedules and can be changed via API or console; Optimize can recommend schedules based on traffic patterns.
20:35 - Liam: about pilot success criteria — we need stable p95 <250ms for inference, no more than 1% error rates, and predictable cost per 1k tokens.
20:46 - Maya: noted, we'll bake those into the pilot SLOs.
20:52 - Samuel: any data residency controls? some of our users are EU-only.
20:58 - Diego: you can pin projects to regions; for Private we can deploy in your EU cloud region.
21:08 - Ava: okay, show me the API flow for rotating a project key without downtime.
21:15 - Diego: example: create new key alias, update clients to use alias, then deprecate old key. Console shows rollouts and usage by key so you can monitor for errors during rotation.
21:32 - Nora: what about rate limits on key creation itself? we have automated processes that create keys dynamically.
21:39 - Diego: there are rate controls on management APIs; for automation we can set higher quotas or service principal flows.
21:46 - Liam: curious about multi-tenant cost attribution — do you split tokens by project for billing?
21:52 - Diego: yes, we track token usage per key/project and provide per-route cost breakdowns. billing can be exported to your billing system.
21:59 - [longer demo step, skipped timestamps]
30:10 - Diego: now an example of a failure policy — when a dedicated lane is full we automatically cascade to a compatible smaller model or queue with a fixed time window.
30:21 - Ethan: do we get metrics for fallback events?
30:25 - Diego: yes, Console emits fallback counts and reasons; Optimize flags regressions when fallback frequency increases.
30:34 - Samuel: for compliance, we need encrypted logs; can you stream logs encrypted to our S3?
30:39 - Diego: yes, encrypted streams are supported and we can deliver to your S3 with customer-managed KMS.
30:48 - Maya: circling back to quotas — recommend pattern: org-level hard cap, project soft caps with burst buckets, priority lanes for latency-critical services, and scheduled policy changes for business hours.
31:05 - Ava: ok that mapping sounds good. can you summarize an architecture diagram for us?
31:11 - Diego: i'll draw up a simple diagram: load balancer -> routing / policy layer -> serving lane (dedicated or shared) -> model runtime. arrows to KMS and audit logs. i'll attach to follow-up.
31:26 - Liam: are there limits on number of project keys? we might have thousands for multi-tenant customers.
31:32 - Diego: Console supports large numbers; we'll discuss scaling patterns for key management (naming, lifecycle automation) in the pilot.
31:44 - Samuel: do you have any pre-built terraform or automation for key provisioning and RBAC?
31:50 - Diego: yes, we have IaC modules and API examples; i'll share terraform snippets after the call.
40:05 - [later in call, Q&A and policy edge cases]
42:12 - Ava: scenario — a rogue process starts hitting a project key, we need immediate containment. how fast can you cut that off?
42:19 - Diego: you can revoke or mute a key in seconds from the console, or configure a threshold-based automatic mute with webhook alerts.
42:31 - Nora: for our platform, we want API keys to be linked to service principals and to rotate nightly. any caveats?
42:38 - Diego: rotation is supported; for high-frequency rotation we recommend using aliases and short-lived tokens issued by your auth layer.
42:50 - Liam: do you support per-key usage anomaly detection?
42:55 - Diego: yes, abnormal usage alerts are part of the observability suite; optimize can surface drift in latencies or token patterns.
43:05 - Samuel: ok looks good. want to confirm support windows and SLA tiers for Dedicated.
43:10 - Maya: Dedicated SLAs are in the enterprise packet; we'll include a summary in the SOW.
43:18 - Diego: quick note: for private or on-prem we also provide a packaging for air-gapped setups with an ops playbook.
43:28 - Ethan: that could be interesting for regulated clients.
50:02 - [closing portion: pilot planning and logistics]
50:12 - Maya: let's align on pilot scope: 4-week pilot, 50 RPS sustained bursts, run both hosted and dedicated variants if possible, measure p95 and fallback rates.
50:24 - Liam: we prefer dedicated for the pilot to see real isolation, but can compare hosted for cost delta.
50:31 - Maya: ok noted. next steps: we'll send pricing and an SOW that includes a pilot plan and an SLA addendum.
50:40 - Samuel: security questionnaire — we'll start that and expect some follow-ups.
50:46 - Maya: we'll share our SOC2 and a redacted architecture diagram.
50:52 - Nora: when can diego run the perf harness?
50:55 - Diego: i'll run it next week once you provide sample prompts and keys; target to deliver results by 2027-11-12.
51:05 - Ava: schedule the pilot kickoff 2027-11-15 morning ET, we'll confirm internally.
51:12 - Maya: perfect, i'll coordinate calendar invites.
51:17 - Ethan: any blockers on our side? i think samuel will own security, nora will provide traffic patterns, and liam will sign off.
51:26 - Samuel: yes i'll get the questionnaire started.
51:31 - Maya: great, final quick notes — we'll include hard cap defaults and a sample policy template in the follow-up.
51:39 - Liam: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
51:43 - Ava: thanks, bye.
51:46 - Diego: thanks all.
62:10 - [call end]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (KMS vs kms, kvcache spelled variably), names sometimes conflated; audio was clear overall. Links to share in follow up: pricing deck, SOW template, benchmark CSV, terraform snippets, security docs.
